title: God Snapshot Events (Mega-Event Overload)
pattern: Publishing the entire deep object graph or system state snapshot on every tiny state change, ignoring the exact delta or semantic event.
why_bad: Creates immense serialization and network transmission overhead. Emitting a 2MB snapshot event to notify subscribers of a single status change wastes bandwidth and memory. It also exposes private, internal state fields of the aggregate that subscribers should not know or depend on.
detection: Observe event types containing large, complex object trees representing the entire aggregate state, emitted for trivial, simple status or flag mutations.
counterexample: Read-model synchronization strategies (such as event sourcing snapshots) that explicitly require capturing full state to speed recovery.
fix:
Emit semantic delta events that communicate only the exact attributes altered by the operation, coupled with the root identity.
```rust
struct OrderStatusChanged {
    order_id: u64,
    new_status: OrderStatus,
}
```
source: *Vaughn Vernon - Implementing Domain-Driven Design (2013)*, Chapter 8, "Domain Events" (Event Serializers / Event Immutability, p. 261); *Martin Kleppmann - Designing Data-Intensive Applications (2017)*, Chapter 11.
